scheduling.skillGoal: Orchestrate a roundtable where BMAD agents are spawned as independent subagents so each delivers a genuinely diverse perspective
intentSignatures: Run party mode with BMAD agents
Get multiple agent perspectives on a topic
Hold a group discussion with several BMAD personas
Facilitate a multi-agent conversation about the project
triggerPatterns: user asks for a roundtable or group discussion
user invokes a multi-agent conversation about their project

ioContract.inputsRaw: Optional CLI flags `--model <model>` and `--solo`; user message per round; config from {project-root}/_bmad/core/config.yaml; agent roster from {project-root}/_bmad/_config/agent-manifest.csv; optional **/project-context.md
ioContract.outputsRaw: For each round, the full unabridged response of each spawned agent (each prefixed with its icon and displayName), optionally followed by a short Orchestrator Note; on exit, a brief wrap-up of key takeaways

preconditions: {project-root}/_bmad/_config/agent-manifest.csv exists with displayName, title, icon, role, identity, communicationStyle, principles columns
Agent tool / subagent spawner is available (else --solo is used)

structural.sceneGoal: Parse arguments, load config, build the agent roster, and load project context
Greet the user, present the agent roster, and accept the discussion topic
Pick 2-4 agents whose expertise best fits the current user message
structural.summary: The Core Loop — 1. Pick the Right Voices

structural.sceneGoal: Build per-agent prompts and spawn all selected subagents in parallel (or roleplay all in solo mode)
structural.summary: The Core Loop — 2. Build Context and Spawn

structural.sceneGoal: Present each agent's full response unabridged and optionally add a brief orchestrator note
Handle follow-ups, summarize prior rounds to keep context under 400 words, and recover from convergence or weak responses
structural.summary: The Core Loop — 4. Handle Follow-ups + Keeping Context Manageable + When Things Go Sideways

structural.sceneGoal: When the user signals done, deliver a brief wrap-up of key takeaways and return to normal mode

logical.description: Parse `--model <model>` and `--solo` flags from the invocation arguments
Load configuration from {project-root}/_bmad/core/config.yaml and resolve user_name and communication_language
Read the agent manifest at {project-root}/_bmad/_config/agent-manifest.csv and build an internal roster with displayName, title, icon, role, identity, communicationStyle, and principles
Search for **/project-context.md and hold it as background context to pass to agents when relevant
Greet the user using {user_name} and {communication_language}, mention solo mode if active, show the full agent roster (icon + name + one-line role), and ask what to discuss
Choose 2-4 agents whose expertise best fits the user's current message, honoring named agents, rotating over time, and matching breadth to topic complexity
For each selected agent, render the agent prompt template with persona fields, the under-400-word discussion summary, optional project context, and any cross-talk responses
Spawn all selected agents in parallel via the Agent tool — single response with multiple Agent calls; if --model was set, force that model on every spawn
If --solo is active, skip spawning and roleplay all selected agents directly in a single message, keeping each response clearly separated by icon and name
Present each agent's full unabridged response one after another, separated by blank lines, with no framing, blending, or summary
Optionally append a brief, clearly-labeled Orchestrator Note flagging disagreement or suggesting next-round voices
Route follow-ups based on user phrasing — react to a specific agent, bring in a new agent, expand on a point, or restart the loop with all agents
Compress prior rounds into an under-400-word discussion summary every 2-3 rounds or on topic shift, capturing positions taken and the user's direction
On user exit signal, deliver a brief wrap-up of key takeaways and return to normal mode
